key_insight: Legendre-based modified extreme learning machines deliver higher accuracy and shorter solution times than tested PINNs for steady-state and discrete-time convection–diffusion benchmarks without iterative gradient-based training.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers efficient simulation of convection-dominated transport with steep gradients and sharp boundary layers.
method: Represent solutions using shifted Legendre polynomial bases.
Determine output weights through a single linear least-squares solve.
Reuse the coefficient-matrix LU or QR factorization across discrete time steps.
evidence_signal: Evaluation covers steady and unsteady benchmarks at relatively high Peclet numbers, continuous and discontinuous boundary conditions, FEM reference solutions, and PINNs with advanced training strategies.
watch_item: Global continuous-time MELM becomes computationally demanding as the space–time basis grows; PINNs show better scalability in this setting.
paper_title: A Legendre-Based Modified Extreme Learning Machine for Convection-Diffusion Equations: Steady-State, Continuous-Time, and Discrete-Time Formulations
